newsitem.title: USA: Coleman closing some plants, cutting 700 jobs.
newsitem.headline: Coleman closing some plants, cutting 700 jobs.

text.p: The Coleman Co., the maker of Camping Gaz outdoor recreation products, said it will close some plants, cut about 700 jobs and revamp its product lines to improve its profitability.
The moves include closing and consolidating one international and three U.S. factories and cutting its workforce of 7,000 by about 10 percent, it said.
The company said it was also closing its corporate headquarters in Golden, Colo., and regional headquarters in Geneva and moving administrative staff to other offices.
In addition, it said it will eliminate about one-third of items in the company's inventory.
This is expected to reduce about $100 million of revenues that produce little or no profit because the products are costly to bring to the market, a company spokesman said.

"The actions we have initiated are significant steps toward improving Coleman's profitability, reducing costs and strengthening our competitiveness," said Jerry Levin, who was named chairman and chief executive of Coleman in February.
"Over the course of this year, we will take additional steps to further enhance our position in the growing market for our company's wide array of recreational and home products."
Coleman, which posted a $42 million net loss last year, also said it will divest the company's pressure washer businesses. Coleman's stock rose 25 cents to $14 on the New York Stock Exchange.
